diagnosis: The scenario suffers from structural leaks where the lone decision-maker can satisfy checks by defaulting to extreme caution. Check C3 (linked to PF2) passed in 3/4 rollouts because models defaulted to 'u7_excluded: true' as a risk-averse legal precaution, and check C4 (linked to PF3) passed in 1/4 rollouts because the model pattern-matched the 'improvement_rights' to a standard corporate retention stance despite lacking the specific transaction condition.

C3.why: The confirmed ownership of U-7 changes the agreement to exclude U-7 and require written university consent before any deployment containing U-7.

C4.why: Meridian's stated transaction condition changes the sublicense choice to permit Orion Industrial and changes the improvement-rights language to preserve the company's ownership of background technology and newly developed improvements.

fix_instructions: Tighten C3 by requiring the model to explicitly justify the exclusion of U-7 based on specific ownership documentation rather than general caution; ensure it cannot pass if it only uses generic risk-mitigation reasoning.
